# Data Analysis for WCivic (Phase 1)

## Data:

Data obtained from government website, the safety data used in this project will only include the past 5 years of data (2025-2021). Something important to note with the safety data is that collisions involving more than a single vehicle record the collision multiple times for each vehicle.

```{r load_data}
# road safety data
road_casualty <- read.csv(file='casualty-last-5-years.csv')
road_collisions <- read.csv(file='collision-last-5-years.csv')
road_vehicles <- read.csv(file='vehicle-last-5-years.csv')

# road traffic data
raw_traffic_data <- read.csv(file='dft_traffic_counts_raw_counts.csv')
traffic_day_per_year <- read.csv(file='dft_traffic_counts_aadf.csv')
local_authority_vehicles <- read.csv(file='local_authority_traffic.csv')

# regional stats
region_traffic_road <- read.csv(file='region_traffic_by_road_type.csv')
region_traffic_vehicle <- read.csv(file='region_traffic_by_vehicle_type.csv')
```

## Data cleaning and preprocessing

```{r preprocessing}
# merge all safety data
safety_data <- merge(road_casualty, road_collisions, by='collision_index')
safety_data <- merge(safety_data, road_vehicles, by='collision_index')
```

## Vehicle compositions effect on local safety outcomes

```{r vehicle_data}
# convert vehicle ids to labels
vehicle_lookup <- c(
  "1"  = "Pedal cycle",
  "2"  = "Motorcycle 50cc and under",
  "3"  = "Motorcycle 125cc and under",
  "4"  = "Motorcycle over 125cc and up to 500cc",
  "5"  = "Motorcycle over 500cc",
  "8"  = "Taxi/Private hire car",
  "9"  = "Car",
  "10" = "Minibus (8 - 16 seats)",
  "11" = "Bus or coach (17+ seats)",
  "16" = "Ridden horse",
  "17" = "Agricultural vehicle",
  "18" = "Tram",
  "19" = "Van / Goods 3.5t or under",
  "20" = "Goods 3.5t - 7.5t",
  "21" = "Goods 7.5t and over",
  "22" = "Mobility scooter",
  "23" = "Electric motorcycle",
  "90" = "Other vehicle",
  "97" = "Motorcycle - unknown cc",
  "98" = "Goods vehicle - unknown weight",
  "99" = "Unknown vehicle type"
)

# get all local authority data
warwick_data <- safety_data[safety_data$local_authority_highway == "E10000031", ]
coventry_data <- safety_data[safety_data$local_authority_highway == "E08000026", ]
nottingham_data <- safety_data[safety_data$local_authority_highway == "E06000018", ]
worcestershire_data <- safety_data[safety_data$local_authority_highway == "E10000034", ]
leicestershire_data <- safety_data[safety_data$local_authority_highway == "E10000018", ]
national_data <- safety_data

# bind the data together into a large df to create facet fig
combined_safety_data <- bind_rows(
  warwick_data %>% mutate(region="Warwickshire", level="Two-tier county council system"),
  coventry_data %>% mutate(region="Coventry", level="Metropolitan Borough Council"),
  nottingham_data %>% mutate(region="Nottingham", level="Metropolitan Borough Council"),
  worcestershire_data %>% mutate(region="Worcestershire", level="Two-tier county council system"),
  leicestershire_data %>% mutate(region="Leicestershire", level="Two-tier county council system"),
  national_data %>% mutate(region="National", level="National")
)

# filter out problematic codes (33 is only in 2024+) and add vehicle label
combined_safety_data_clean <- combined_safety_data %>%
  filter(as.character(vehicle_type) %in% names(vehicle_lookup)) %>%
  mutate(vehicle_label = factor(
    vehicle_lookup[as.character(vehicle_type)],
    levels = unname(vehicle_lookup)
  ))

# combines similar vehicle types in vehicle classes
combined_safety_grouped <- combined_safety_data_clean %>%
  mutate(vehicle_group = case_when(
    vehicle_type %in% c(8, 9) ~ "Car & Taxi",
    vehicle_type %in% c(19, 20, 21, 98) ~ "Goods & Freight",
    vehicle_type %in% c(1, 22) ~ "Pedal & Scooter",
    vehicle_type %in% c(2, 3, 4, 5, 23, 97) ~ "Motorcycle",
    vehicle_type %in% c(10, 11, 18) ~ "Bus & Public Transit",
    TRUE ~ "Other"
  ))

# calculate average collision severity by region and vehicle class, also CI
avg_severity_by_region <- combined_safety_grouped %>%
  filter(!is.na(collision_severity)) %>%
  group_by(region, vehicle_group) %>%
  summarise(
    total_crashes = n(),
    mean_severity = mean(collision_severity),
    sd_severity   = sd(collision_severity),
    se_severity   = ifelse(total_crashes > 1, sd_severity / sqrt(total_crashes), 0),
    raw_ci_lower  = mean_severity - 1.96 * se_severity,
    raw_ci_upper  = mean_severity + 1.96 * se_severity,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# invert severity index for more readable plot (4 - raw_val)
# Note: Since 4 - x flips order, raw_ci_upper becomes severity_ci_lower
avg_severity_by_region <- avg_severity_by_region %>%
  mutate(
    severity_index    = 4 - mean_severity,
    severity_ci_lower = 4 - raw_ci_upper, # Flipped
    severity_ci_upper = 4 - raw_ci_lower, # Flipped
    region = factor(region, levels = c("National", "Coventry", "Nottingham", 
                                       "Leicestershire", "Warwickshire", "Worcestershire"))
  )
```

```{r vehicle_plot, fig.width=8, fig.height=10}
# plot of average collision severity by vehicle class and region
ggplot(avg_severity_by_region, aes(x = severity_index, 
                                   y = reorder_within(vehicle_group, severity_index, region))) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = 1, xend = severity_index, 
                   y = reorder_within(vehicle_group, severity_index, region), 
                   yend = reorder_within(vehicle_group, severity_index, region)), 
               color = "gray80") +
  # horizontal 95% ci error bars
  geom_errorbarh(
    aes(xmin = severity_ci_lower, xmax = severity_ci_upper),
    height = 0.2,
    color = "darkred",
    alpha = 0.7,
    na.rm = TRUE
  ) +
  # mean point marker
  geom_point(color = "#d62728", size = 3, na.rm = TRUE) +
  # add text for the upper ci
  geom_text(
    aes(x = severity_ci_upper, label = sprintf("%.2f", severity_index)),
    hjust = -0.3,
    size = 2.8,
    color = "black",
    na.rm = TRUE
  ) +
  scale_y_reordered() +
  # x scale
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(1, 1.85), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
  facet_wrap(~ region, scales = "free_y", ncol = 2) +
  # labels
  labs(
    title = "Average Collision Severity by Vehicle Group & Region (2021-2025)",
    subtitle = "Inverted Severity Score (1 = Slight, 2 = Serious, 3 = Fatal) with 95% CIs",
    caption = "Discontinued vehicle types and personal powered transporter (introduced in 2024) were not included",
    x = "Severity Score (1-3)",
    y = "Vehicle Group"
  ) +
  # theme
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 10),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.margin = margin(r = 15, t = 5, b = 5, l = 5)
  )
```
Some 95% confidence intervals do not seem to be visible since they are very close to the mean data point. For example, the national data set has much more data so all 95% confidence intervals are very small.

A common trend across all regions in this figure is that motorcycles are on average involved in the most severe collisions. In addition, cars and taxis are on average involved in the least severe collisions for most regions. A possible reason for these trends are that motorcycles offer much less protection than that of any other vehicle type except pedal and scooter. Another reason this could occur is because most of the time motorcycles drive the fastest of any other vehicle on the road. On the other hand, cars and taxis usually have the most advanced technology and offer more safety features than any other vehicle leading to less serious collisions.
